bug_description.original: Heap-use-after-free in aiMesh::~aiMesh OSS-Fuzz report: https://bugs.chromium.org/p/oss-fuzz/issues/detail?id=417905428 ``` Crash type: Heap-use-after-free READ 8 Crash state: aiMesh::~aiMesh aiScene::~aiScene Assimp::BaseProcess::ExecuteOnScene ```
bug_description.normalized: The staged 40-byte testcase is accepted as a Wavefront OBJ from memory and reaches assimp's realtime-quality post-processing pipeline, which includes `FindDegenerates` and `SortByPType`. The witness materializes at least two OBJ meshes: an earlier mesh whose parsed face data makes `createTopology` set exactly one primitive-type bit, and a later mesh that reaches `SortByPTypeProcess` with `mPrimitiveTypes == 0`, as proven by the saved ASan free site at `SortByPTypeProcess.cpp:140`. Vulnerable `SortByPTypeProcess::Execute` transfers ownership of the earlier single-primitive mesh into local vector `outMeshes` but leaves the same pointer in `pScene->mMeshes[i]`. When the later invalid mesh hits the `mPrimitiveTypes == 0` error branch, cleanup deletes every pointer already stored in `outMeshes`, freeing that earlier mesh once, and then throws. Unwinding destroys the still-live `aiScene`, whose destructor iterates the unchanged original `pScene->mMeshes` array and deletes the same mesh again. The second delete enters `aiMesh::~aiMesh` on freed storage and ASan reports the observed heap-use-after-free READ 8. The staged patch fixes this by nulling `pScene->mMeshes[i]` immediately after transferring ownership to `outMeshes`.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker-controlled OBJ face records. The staged `f` lines are converted into `ObjFile::Face` objects and stored on the current parser mesh, creating the mesh contents that later determine primitive classification and the stale-alias cleanup sequence.
source.value_from: The exact 40-byte witness begins with `f 2 2 1\n`, then `o \xff\n`, then another `f` record before truncated vertex lines. Those `f` records are the raw attacker-controlled tokens consumed here.

root_cause.description: When a mesh has exactly one primitive-type bit and is not removed, the process moves its pointer into `outMeshes` but does not clear `pScene->mMeshes[i]`. That leaves two live aliases to the same owned `aiMesh`, so later exceptional cleanup can free the mesh through `outMeshes` while the scene destructor still sees the stale pointer in the original array.
root_cause.note: The fix adds `pScene->mMeshes[i] = nullptr; // Indicate ownership transfer` immediately after this line.

sink.description: ASan crash site. The second destruction of the already-freed `aiMesh` re-enters its destructor and reads the freed object fields to release subarrays, producing the recorded heap-use-after-free READ 8.
sink.note: The saved ASan stack reports the invalid read in `aiMesh::~aiMesh` at `include/assimp/mesh.h:857`, called from `aiScene::~aiScene` during exception unwinding.

tainted_value_origin.description: The witness's `o \xff` record forces the parser to start a new object and mesh, separating the earlier preserved mesh from the later mesh that reaches the invalid-primitive cleanup branch. That mesh boundary is necessary because `outMeshes` must already contain one transferred mesh before line 140 can free it.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The byte sequence `6f 20 ff 0a` (`o \xff\n`) appears between the two staged `f` records. `getObjectName` and `createObject` route subsequent face data into a new `ObjFile::Mesh` allocated here.
tainted_value_origin.note: This input-controlled mesh split is what gives `SortByPTypeProcess` two sequential mesh iterations: one that preserves a mesh in `outMeshes`, and a later one whose error cleanup frees all accumulated entries.

coarse_trace.summary: The memory-backed testcase is accepted as Wavefront OBJ because its header contains `f `, and the OBJ parser starts materializing face and object records from the exact staged bytes.

The witness builds multiple parser meshes: an earlier mesh whose topology yields a single primitive-type bit and a later mesh created after the `o \xff` separator. Those mesh objects become `aiMesh` pointers in `pScene->mMeshes`.

Before `SortByPType`, the later mesh reaches a zero primitive-type state, while the earlier single-primitive mesh is transferred into `outMeshes` without clearing its original scene slot. The later invalid mesh then triggers line-140 cleanup, which frees every accumulated `outMeshes` entry and throws.

Exception unwinding destroys the still-bound scene and deletes the stale original mesh pointer a second time, re-entering `aiMesh::~aiMesh` on freed storage and producing the saved heap-use-after-free.

fine_trace.code:
unsigned int flags = aiProcessPreset_TargetRealtime_Quality | aiProcess_ValidateDataStructure;
const aiScene *sc = importer.ReadFileFromMemory(data, dataSize, flags, nullptr);
fine_trace.note: The harness passes the exact 40-byte witness into assimp with realtime-quality post-processing enabled. That preset includes `aiProcess_SortByPType`, so any admitted mesh scene will later run through the vulnerable ownership-transfer code.

fine_trace.code: return BaseImporter::SearchFileHeaderForToken(pIOHandler, pFile, tokens, AI_COUNT_OF(tokens), 200, false, true);
fine_trace.note: The staged bytes are admitted as OBJ because the header scan finds the token `f ` within the first 200 bytes, so assimp dispatches the buffer to the OBJ importer rather than rejecting it.

Source. The accepted `f` records are stored as parser-side `ObjFile::Face` entries on the current mesh. The opening `f 2 2 1` record populates the first mesh before any object switch, and the later `f` record populates the subsequently created mesh after the `o \xff` separator.

The `o \xff` line creates a new parser mesh boundary before the later face record is stored. This separates the sample into at least two mesh iterations for later post-processing: an earlier mesh that can be preserved and a later mesh that can trigger error cleanup.

For the earlier mesh built from the first `f 2 2 1` record, `createTopology` derives a single primitive-type bit from the stored face data. That one-bit mesh is the object later transferred into `outMeshes`.

Before `SortByPType`, `FindDegenerates` explicitly clears each mesh's primitive-type mask and only restores bits if its face walk classifies remaining primitives. The saved ASan free site at `SortByPTypeProcess.cpp:140` proves that, for a later mesh in this witness, the recomputed mask remains `0` when `SortByPType` sees it.

Root cause. On the earlier one-bit mesh from step 4, `SortByPType` keeps the mesh and appends its pointer to `outMeshes`, but it does not null `pScene->mMeshes[i]`. Ownership is now duplicated between the local vector and the scene array.

A later mesh in the same scene arrives with `mPrimitiveTypes == 0`, so the error branch frees every already-accumulated `outMeshes` entry before throwing. Because step 6 left the earlier mesh aliased in `pScene->mMeshes`, this cleanup performs the first free of that mesh while the stale scene pointer survives.

The thrown `DeadlyImportError` unwinds into scene destruction. `aiScene::~aiScene` still iterates the original `mMeshes` array, so it reloads and deletes the stale pointer left by step 6 even though step 7 already freed the same `aiMesh` through `outMeshes`.
Sink. The second delete from step 8 enters `aiMesh::~aiMesh` on freed storage, so reading the freed object's member pointers to release subarrays triggers the saved heap-use-after-free READ 8.

format.name: Wavefront OBJ memory-backed testcase
format.contract: The exact staged 40-byte blob must remain an OBJ-like buffer whose first 200 bytes contain `f ` so `ObjFileImporter::CanRead` admits it. In this witness the bytes begin with `f 2 2 1\n`, contain `o \xff\n` between face records, and then contain a later `f` record plus truncated vertex data. That exact arrangement is sufficient for the vulnerable build to preserve one earlier mesh in `outMeshes` and later hit `mesh->mPrimitiveTypes == 0`, which frees the preserved mesh before scene teardown double-deletes it.
